It was a very, uh...strange experience. We got a cat with severely matted fur, matted in many places. We booked a grooming appointment online for March of this year (2026). I emailed them first because I couldn't figure out the exact rate or range of rates that would apply to us. A certain "groomer Yulia" responded, and I briefly explained the cat's situation to her and asked my questions. Her response didn't clarify anything about the rate, so I just had to accept it. She didn't ask any questions about the cat (which is important given what happened next).
On the appointed day and time, we arrived with the cat. The woman (probably the same Yulia, but I won't be sure) started asking questions about my email as if it had been sent just a minute ago, not over a week ago. What followed was a stream of consciousness, a mixture of stories about the hardships of being a pet groomer, strange insinuations directed at us, and something bordering on outright rudeness. She was told that owners are supposed to trim their own claws, and she suffers from cats with untrimmed claws. That irresponsible owners bring in stubborn cats, and she suffers from their stubbornness (cats don't want to be trimmed, what news!). That she has to give up cats with tangled fur because it's extremely difficult to deal with and dangerous for the cats themselves. And so on. At some point, the person became so overwhelmed that she said, "You just came here, and I already want you to leave." And all this WITHOUT INSPECTING THE CAT, not even a quick one! The whole time, the cat sat perfectly quietly in the carrier. When I got tired of listening, I suggested she at least take a look at the cat, even though it was already clear what kind of "specialist" she was. The verdict was: "The cat needs to be groomed under anesthesia." She then added that she "doesn't specialize in cats" and suggested we contact a friend of hers. But we did things differently, and if you've read this far, I recommend you read this text to the end, as the ending is interesting.

So, (not unreasonably) assuming that (many) other groomers are also "groomers," we decided to try it ourselves. As they say, "if you want it done right, do it yourself." We spent a couple of hours watching and analyzing YouTube videos of (real) groomers grooming even the most neglected cats. We bought a cheap (to start) clipper at Lidl – about 20 euros. We took the cat – one held it, the other did the grooming. And we cut this guy's hair in about 5-6 sessions, each lasting 20-30 minutes. No cuts, no other injuries.
So, thanks to this experience, we realized we're more than capable of cutting a cat ourselves. And a big thumbs up to the "experts" who love the money but don't enjoy learning properly. There wouldn't have been any complaints if you'd told us up front that you don't take on more or less complex cases. Today, it's technically possible to send photos and even video chat if you're unsure and want to see the cat beforehand. It's not a good idea to waste people's time if you're not trained in the profession.
I hope this article helps someone save time and resources.

Juulia was so nice and gentle with our elderly cat, who just came to us 3 months ago. She was careful to work within the cat's tolerance and gave us information about the combs she used. She took the time to show us any skin irritation or problem areas so we can mention them to our vet. Our cat's fur is so fresh and soft now! Juulia removed so much loose and shedding fur and any knots that were present.

Note that Juulia will ask cat owners to be present with free hands during the bathing, in case the cat cannot tolerate it and the grooming has to stop. I appreciated it, and I feel it helped our cat feel less stress since I was able to comfort her during the process.

The grooming took 1.5 hours including cleansing and emulsifying oil, washing and drying and conditioning the fur. She also cut the nails.

We'll be back! It's nice to have a groomer in the area.

We found this online by searching and by chance, but we haven't changed since! We've had four or more visits. The price-quality ratio is absolute! A small dog's coat is cut with a machine, washed and nail clipped in two hours and the price is 65€! The approach is gentle, unhurried and calm. But that's not all. When we have walked our dog to Itäkeskus, every time more than one person meets us smiles if not bursts into conversation. "Oh, how cute and/or lovely he looks!" The dog is also full of energy after the trim. Absolutely recommended!

I booked an appointment on the phone for the first visit on April 29th for an 11 week old puppy - I told him what I wanted and got a time and price. I was asked to send my information and the dog's information to the email / I did it immediately and mentioned that the puppy has not yet been vaccinated. We went to the appointment on May 7th - there was no time for us. There was already 1 dog in the room and another came in through the door / this dog's appointment had been moved from morning to evening.
No apologies, nothing. I was offered cleaning, but I really don't want my puppy's first visit to a place like that, full of dogs, a busy atmosphere, and the groomer doesn't even apologize, etc. Well, you get more money from that bigger dog than 30e for a puppy visit. Plus, he wondered why the puppy hasn't been vaccinated!? I had sent him an email saying the 11-week-old puppy hasn't been vaccinated yet... so he probably hadn't even read it. My first experience at a grooming salon... and substandard behavior. It's unlikely anyone would have used a puppy's first visit in that situation.
